programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock

Although he loves the dizzy feeling to begin with, Bing soon realises that it’s not so fun to feel too dizzy!

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Tha Bing a’ togail taigh le cluasagan, gnìomh a tha toirt air Coco geama de ‘Madadh-allaidh Mosach’ a mholadh. Tha e còrdadh ri Bing a bhith leigeil air gur e madadh-allaidh crosta a th’ ann… gus an tuig e nach fhaigh e am broinn an taigh a thog e! Bing has built a house with the sofa cushions, prompting Coco to suggest they all play ‘Big Bad Wolf’ together. Bing is very excited that he gets to be the angry wolf, until he realises that it means he won’t be allowed into the house that he built!

programme.title: Peicein/Petit
programme.desc: Tha caraidean Pheicein ag innse dha mun t-sanas ùr aig “Silidh Milis Steigeach”, ma ghlèidheas tu ochd bileagan bho na mullaich, gheibh thu paidhir spèileachain. ’S e an trioblaid, gu bheil blas grot far “Silidh Milis Steigeach”. Petit finds out if you collect eight Really Tasty Candy lids you get a free pair of roller skates! The only catch is Really Tasty Candy tastes really, really, bad...

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Tha na Pluic a’ ceannach ‘Grodbitan’ airson toirt orra beagan eacarsaich a dhèanamh. Chan fhada gu tuig iad gu bheil rudeigin fada ceàrr air na h-innealan, oir cha ghabh an cuir dheth às dèidh dhaibh uile an cleachdadh. Tha na Pluic ann an staing is gun dòigh aca air stad a dh’eacarsaich. Investing in GritBits to get them moving, the Spuds discover the devices are faulty and cannot be switched off once attached to their wrists. The Spuds quickly find themselves unable to stop exercising.

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Tha Pòl a’ cuideachadh cailleach air a bheil Tilidh, is tha i a’ toirt isbean dha mar thaing. An e mac-meanmna Phòil a th’ ann, no a bheil rudeigin fortanach a’ tachairt le gach greim a ghabhas e dhen isbean? Dave helps a local old lady called Tanya, who rewards him by giving him a sausage to say thank you. Is Dave imagining it or does something lucky happen every time he takes a bite?

programme.title: Hilda
programme.desc: Chan eil iad a' creidsinn anns a' Cheann a Tuath g’ eil na h-aithrisean aig Artair fìor. Tha fear air nochdadh airson àit’ a ghabhail. Chan eil Artair deònach Trolberg fhàgail. Dè nì e? In the Northern Colonies, they don’t believe that Artair’s reports are true. Someone has come to take his place. Artair isn’t willing to leave Trolberg. What will he do?

programme.title: An Sgoil
programme.desc: Ged a tha na saor-làithean air tòiseachadh do sgoilearan Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche, tha latha a bharrachd aig an luchd-teagaisg airson beagan trèanaidh. Tha an t-eòlaiche-inntinn Sìleas Stern os cionn sheiseanan gus sìth agus càirdeas a stèidheachadh am measg an luchd-obrach. Although the holidays have started for the pupils of Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche, the teachers have an in-service day. Mr Mackle is keen to establish better relationships between his staff and has invited psychologist Sìleas Stern to run team building sessions that he hopes will bring peace and harmony.

programme.title: Samhradh air Sàl
programme.desc: Angus Mackay is joined by longtime friend and colleague Tormod Macleod from Carloway as they go to sea for a day’s fishing off the east coast of Lewis. Along the way they encounter sea eagles and enjoy an environment lit by the sunshine of a beautiful summer’s day. Along the way they ponder the importance of fishing on family ties. Tha Tormod MacLeòid à Càrlabhagh – deagh charaid agus co-obraiche Aonghas MhicAoidh – còmhla ris agus iad a’ dol gu muir airson latha iasgaich far costa an ear Leòdhais. Coinnichidh iad ri iolairean-mara agus a’ ghrian a’ deàrrsadh air latha samhraidh brèagha. Air an t-slighe, tha iad a’ meòrachadh air cho cudromach ’s a tha iasgach do cheanglaichean teaghlaich.

programme.title: Voyages of Discovery
programme.desc: Explorer Paul Rose tells the story of one of the greatest ever sea adventures, which transformed Captain James Cook into a national hero and dramatically changed the course of history. Two and a half centuries later, Captain Cook is still a household name, but his achievements are often misunderstood, contrary to popular perception, he did not discover New Zealand and Australia. Intrepid Rose follows his journey down under and uncovers the real story of Captain Cook.

programme.title: The Interview
programme.desc: David Hockney was one of the world's most successful and influential artists of our time. At 11, he wanted to be an artist. At 87, he was still creating new works - happiest when making 'joyful' art and always innovating with his iPad. His art has sold for millions. In a film originally broadcast in April 2025, ahead of his biggest show ever opening in Paris, the Bradford-born star talks to Katie Razzall about growing old, a recent visit from the King and his two big loves - smoking and painting.

programme.title: Face to Face
programme.desc: In an interview first broadcast in 1996, artist David Hockney talks to Jeremy Isaacs about painting, designing for the opera and his growing deafness.

programme.title: Natural World
programme.desc: Looking at the secret lives of the wildlife in one of Britain's favourite gardens. Shot by Charlie Hamilton-James, this film follows various animals, from the family of foxes that play after hours in the pleasure gardens to the toads in the Italian garden and the badgers that clear up the tea rooms at night. Set against the background of the gardening year, these stories reveal life behind the scenes at Heligan.

programme.title: Inside Classical
programme.desc: The BBC Philharmonic Orchestra, led by Ludovic Morlot, presents a concert celebrating spring’s extraordinary creative power as a season of renewal and rebirth, through evocative lighting and musical soundscapes, from Manchester’s Aviva Studios. Presented by Ben Gernon. Igor Stravinsky’s ballet score The Rite of Spring, which famously incited audience uproar in its 1913 Paris premiere, is an exhilarating start to the programme. With its asymmetrical rhythms, brutal harmonies and sonic aggression, it continues to fascinate audiences today and remains one of the most influential works of the 20th century. The UK premiere of Jessie Montgomery’s Chemiluminescence follows in calm contrast. This work for string orchestra introduces an atmosphere of contemplative beauty as science and the natural world are united through sound in the composer’s musical depiction of the creation of light from a non-light source. An evocative programme of musical concepts, exploring spring’s explosive destruction and radiant light.

programme.title: BBC Proms
programme.desc: Two goliaths of 20th-century music, Ravi Shankar and Philip Glass, recorded the studio album Passages together in 1989. The result was a unique fusion of Hindustani sitar music with American minimalism. Tonight the album is performed live and in full for the first time, with Shankar's daughter Anoushka playing the sitar alongside a dazzling array of Indian soloists and the Britten Sinfonia, conducted by Karen Kamensek.

programme.title: In Concert
programme.desc: Concert featuring Indian musician Ravi Shankar, first shown in 1974. He performs just one song, entitled Rag Behag.

programme.title: South Asian Music at the BBC
programme.desc: To help mark 60 years of Asian broadcasting at the BBC, DJ Bobby Friction shares his love and knowledge of South Asian music with a journey back through the archives that celebrates some of the genre’s most important, enduring and spectacular acts from across the decades. With artists ranging from Lata Mangeshkar, Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan and Ravi Shankar right through to Asian Dub Foundation, Naughty Boy and Apache Indian, Bobby’s selection highlights the vast range of musical styles and sounds, as well as the unbridled joy that feels built into so many of the performances that he’s personally selected.

programme.title: Rachel Khoo's Kitchen Notebook
programme.desc: Cook and food writer Rachel Khoo visits the cool of Sweden's capital city to continue her culinary journey. Rachel visits one of Stockholm's hippest restaurants, where rump of deer is on the menu. Back home, she's inspired by Sweden's traditional cinnamon buns and bakes her own savoury Swedish buns as well as cooking venison steak with celeriac puree, pickled blackberries and carrot petals and a lingonberry and raspberry marzipan tart, inspired by the Swedish lingonberry.

programme.title: Talking Movies
programme.desc: To mark America's 250th anniversary, Talking Movies hears from leading figures in US media, film and culture who tell the BBC about some iconic American movies and what these films reveal about the country and the psyche of her people. American Psycho director Mary Harron talks about Martin Scorsese's The King of Comedy, while critic and film-maker Bilge Ebiri looks at Hitchcock's classic thriller North by Northwest. BBC News presenter Sumi Somaskanda reveals her passion for the prison drama The Shawshank Redemption and award-winning journalist Tim Teeman selects Steven Spielberg's Jaws. Talking Movies' host Tom Brook chooses the Robert Altman ensemble satire Nashville. Each contributor speaks about what their film choice means to them and how and why they feel it has become an American cinema classic. This special illustrates the American nation on the big screen and the influence it's had in bringing its movies to the world.

programme.title: AI Decoded
programme.desc: The race between America and China to lead the world in artificial intelligence is reshaping the global balance of power. But behind the headlines, a hidden conflict is unfolding. Join AI Decoded as we examine the seizure of $13 million worth of advanced AI chips allegedly bound for China, and Anthropic's claim that Alibaba carried out the largest known AI 'distillation attack' in history. As nations and tech giants compete for supremacy, the battle for AI is increasingly being fought in the shadows. Who will win the race for AI dominance, and how far will they go to get there?

programme.title: BBC Wales Investigates
programme.desc: You could be a scroll away from finding a sperm donor. But at what cost? With fertility prices soaring and treatment difficult to access for some, same-sex female couples say they have little choice but to turn to social media to make a baby. Social media groups and apps are fuelling a cheap, easy and totally unregulated donor market. But it’s risky: outside of a sperm clinic, there’s no guarantee of health screening, and you’re not legally protected. And it’s not just a gamble for those wanting to get pregnant. According to the UK’s fertility regulator, men who donate sperm outside of clinics may also be breaking the law if they’re storing, processing or sending sperm. But what do they think of this? Meet the men travelling the world to donate sperm, and find out what happens when reporter Gemma Dunstan tries to order a sample online.

programme.title: China's Greatest Treasures
programme.desc: Music and dance in China enjoy a fascinatingly long lineage dating back to at least 3000 BC. Ancient documents reveal countless forms of music and dance in connection with religious rituals, folk festivals and everyday life. Alastair explores some of the most iconic forms of ancient Chinese music and dance and also discovers how they are celebrated and kept alive today.

programme.title: Prayer and Reflection
programme.desc: Guru Nanak Darbar Gurdwara in Gravesend in Kent – the UK’s largest Sikh temple – invites us to join their daily prayers and services. At 4.00am, the holy book, called the Guru Granth Sahib, is brought out from its overnight resting place, called the Sachkhand. It’s carried to the Main Diwan (prayer) Hall, where the first of the daily prayers are read. During the course of the morning, worshippers arrive at the temple to join a number of different prayers, including Japji Sahib (prayer from holy text), Asa di Var (hymn), Katha (sermon), Ardas (standing prayer) and Hukamnama (command). There is also the conclusion (Bhog) of a 48-hour prayer known as the Akhand Paath, a nonstop reading of the entire Guru Granth Sahib, Sikhism's sacred scripture. We also witness a core element of Sikhism called Sewa, or selfless service. Every morning at first light, volunteers arrive in the Langar (food) hall of the Gurdwara to prepare food for the congregation throughout the course of the day.

programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.desc: As we enjoy the summer months, Pam Rhodes visits Ashburnham Place Retreat Centre in East Sussex to introduce a feast of much-loved hymns that explore the profound meaning of water in the Bible and in the expression of Christian faith. Surrounded by acres of ancient woodland and glorious lakes, Ashburnham Place provides a peaceful setting for Pam to reflect on the profound significance of water in the scriptures – from the story of creation to Jesus offering the water of eternal life. Pam also tells stories of composers for whom water proved a source of inspiration, with hymns and worship songs from across the UK, including Here Is Love Vast as the Ocean, performed by Unoma Okudo; I Heard the Voice of Jesus Say, from Our Lady's Church, York; and Like a Mighty River Flowing, from St George’s Church in Jesmond. Also featured are: O the Deep, Deep Love of Jesus, from St David's Church, Exeter; Rain, led by Noel Robinson at the Church of Christ the Cornerstone, Milton Keynes; and As the Deer Pants for Water, from Inverness Cathedral.

Surrounded by acres of ancient woodland and glorious lakes, Ashburnham Place provides a peaceful setting for Pam to reflect on the profound significance of water in the scriptures – from the story of creation to Jesus offering the water of eternal life. Pam also tells stories of composers for whom water proved a source of inspiration, with hymns and worship songs from across the UK, including Here Is Love Vast as the Ocean, performed by Unoma Okudo; I Heard the Voice of Jesus Say, from Our Lady's Church, York; and Like a Mighty River Flowing, from St George’s Church in Jesmond. Also featured are: O the Deep, Deep Love of Jesus, from St David's Church, Exeter; Rain, led by Noel Robinson at the Church of Christ the Cornerstone, Milton Keynes; and As the Deer Pants for Water, from Inverness Cathedral.

programme.desc: All the weekend national, UK-wide and international news on Sunday evening at 7.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: Prestwick’s Broadway Cinema hasn’t shown a film since its doors closed in 1976, so Mark Stuckey and Steve Rowley must battle rust, missing wires and obsolete carbon-arc lamps if they hope to bring its twin projectors back to life. Dom meets Shetlander Victoria, who needs her grandfather’s accordion fixed if she is to realise her busking ambitions, and then discovers the centuries-old art of enamelling watch dials, a craft that demands steady hands.

programme.title: Island Crossings
programme.desc: Twenty new apprentices join the ranks of CalMac, while Tiree crofters ready their cattle for the final island market of the season, drawing buyers from across Scotland.

programme.title: Paramedics on Scene
programme.desc: Stevie and Pete of the Special Operations Response Team join the other emergency services at the scene of a man who is threatening to harm himself in a public place. It’s a distressing situation that takes a sudden, unexpected turn. Pete must take action to help rescue the patient and deliver him safely to the care of a local ambulance crew. Serving a community of around 9,000 people, Dunoon-based paramedic Ben is used to the occasional quiet shift. But he has a potentially life-threatening emergency in the shape of Ian, who has a blood clot in his lung. It’s vital the team get him across the Firth of Clyde for specialist care at Inverclyde Hospital - but will they make the last ferry of the night? Meanwhile, in Paisley, ambulance technicians Lewis and Steven take stroke patient John to Glasgow’s Queen Elizabeth Hospital for an emergency thrombectomy. But John’s case brings back difficult memories for Steven, who is living with the recent loss of his father in tragically similar circumstances.

programme.title: Still Game
programme.desc: Sitcom featuring characters from comedy series Chewin' the Fat. Jack and Victor, jealous of Old Tam's success at winning prizes by entering catchphrase competitions, decide to come up with a catchy new slogan for scones.

programme.title: Scot Squad
programme.desc: Thrills, spills and lengthy lunch bills as the bold Bravehearts flash the blue light and curtail criminality. Traffic officer Hugh McKirdy regrets going commando - his partner Surjit Singh dutifully provides cover while he seeks reinforcement undergarments. At Coms HQ, there's a promotion for Maggie Le Beau, but the new call centre team leader soon discovers a breakdown in communications. Retired Police Chief Sir Neville Archibald selects the swankiest of eateries for an elongated procedural discussion with Cameron Miekelson. The local cop shop becomes a hotbed of political activity as officer Karen encounters an unstoppable force of passion. Cop comedy cuffing crime in all its guises. Starring Jack Docherty, Grado, Manjot Sumal, ML Stone, Karen Bartke, Darren Connell, Paul Sneddon and special guest Bill Paterson.

programme.title: The Troops
programme.desc: Scots defend trenches in Estonia, while others scout enemy lines and protect HQ. In Catterick, chaos reigns in riot training, while ceremonial troops in Edinburgh fight for redemption.

programme.title: Rooney
programme.desc: The 2022 documentary film giving unprecedented access to the life and career of one of football’s greatest strikers. Wayne Rooney recounts stories from some of the most important moments of his life, with testimonies from the people closest to him, including family, friends and his wife Coleen. From his time as a young boy growing up in the Liverpool district of Croxteth, through to his teenage life where his emerging stardom led to intense scrutiny from the British press, the film places Rooney’s professional career under a microscope, journeying through some of the highest and most challenging moments in the life of England’s record goal scorer. Footballing greats such as David Beckham, Gary Neville, Rio Ferdinand and Thierry Henry illustrate first-hand accounts of Rooney as a teammate and an opponent. Meaningful testimonies from the likes of Rooney’s first Premier League manager, David Moyes, and his first England manager, Sven-Göran Eriksson, describe the seemingly unlimited potential they saw in Rooney at such a young age.

programme.title: Desmond Armstrong: America's World Cup Pioneer
programme.desc: Desmond Armstrong was the first US-born black player to represent the United States men's national football team at a World Cup. He was part of the squad that did the unthinkable: qualifying for Italia 90 at a time when the US had no professional league and football wasn't taken seriously. This documentary explores how he got there, the racial tensions of that era and his work as a youth academy coach in Antioch, Nashville, making the sport accessible to immigrant communities against a backdrop of heightened immigration enforcement.

programme.title: Glorious Gardens from Above
programme.desc: Christine Walkden visits Bodnant Garden in Snowdonia to explore a Himalayan valley amid the mountains of north Wales. She meets Phyllis, who is treading in her grandfather's footsteps. At nearby Bodysgallen Hall, an unexpected view takes her back to childhood holidays. And we hear the story of the building of the Snowdon Mountain Railway.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Charlotte Smith and Joe Crowley mark the 50th anniversary of the Viking Way, exploring the people, wildlife and history connected by Lincolnshire's famous long-distance footpath. They uncover evidence of Viking settlers, meet the volunteers who maintain the route, visit the Ramblers' Church and witness efforts to protect water voles. Adam Henson explores high-tech strawberry farming, and John Craven launches Countryfile's annual photographic competition.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Lizzie Schofield and Brian Cunningham are starting new projects and checking on the progress of planting carried out in previous years. Lizzie is in her herb garden, which she renovated in 2024, assessing what has worked and what needs to be refreshed. Meanwhile, Brian is checking on the apple trees he planted in the spring as examples of espalier shaping and pruning. Lizzie begins plans in the garden for cut flowers that will give her foliage alongside the blooms already beginning to take shape, and Brian is planting more perennials in the terraced patio area. There are all the usual handy hints, as well as a look at what plants are good for attracting birds to your plot.

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: The last programme of the spring series, Dougie and the team are at Ingliston for The Royal Highland Show. Cammy catches up with a professional sheep dresser as he makes finishing touches before showing his Bleu du Maines. As Landward celebrates fifty years on air, Dougie looks back on show coverage from the archive. Rosie gets a taste of Aberdeenshire in the food and drink hall showcasing artisan producers, Arlene visits the honey tent to find about the complexities of judging the amber nectar, Cammy’s hoping to win a red rosette in the show ring with his Jersey dairy cow. And Dougie steps into the main ring to follow the spectacular grand parade.

programme.title: Jane Eyre
programme.desc: Charlotte Bronte's classic about an orphan girl who grows up to become a governess in a gloomy manor in Yorkshire, where she falls in love with the mysterious Edward Rochester.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Anita Rani begins a four-part journey along England’s east coast, exploring the wildlife, landscapes and communities adapting to life on the edge of the sea. Her first stop is Northey Island in Essex, an internationally important refuge for threatened birds, including curlew, lapwing and dunlin. With rising sea levels putting increasing pressure on coastal habitats, Anita discovers an innovative conservation project using retired Thames barges to help protect the island’s future. She also meets the volunteers working to safeguard vulnerable ringed plover nests using a simple but effective solution. Anita also delves into the Countryfile archives to revisit some of the projects helping to create more space for nature to thrive.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow visits one of the grandest, historic houses in Wales, Powis Castle. Duncan Campbell discovers a very rare silver tobacco box from the 1600s, and Serhat Ahmet examines a porcelain egg with a royal connection. Meanwhile, Paul Atterbury is taken back to the earliest days of Doctor Who, while Alexandra Aguilar values a jade ornament bought at a car boot sale for 50 pence. Geoffrey Munn uncovers a jewellery collection ‘of the highest quality’ with rubies and diamonds dating from the 1700s.

programme.title: Amazing Hotels: Life Beyond the Lobby
programme.desc: Rob Rinder and Monica Galetti travel to Turkey to work at Argos in Cappadocia, a hotel built into a network of ancient caves. Combining history with modern luxury, Monica finds herself brushing cave ceilings with housekeeping before flying above in a hot air balloon. Meanwhile, Rob helps with the finishing touches of a new spa. With each room providing surprises and inviting curiosity, Rob seeks further education on the history of the caves as Monica practises centuries-old traditional cooking techniques.

programme.title: Murder Case
programme.desc: A team of detectives arrive in the market town of Elgin tasked with investigating the brutal murder of a 32-year-old mother of two. On 16 November 2023, Lucretia ‘Kiesha’ Donaghy’s body is discovered in her home after worried friends are unable to reach her. She has been victim of a frenzied attack. We follow the detectives' every move as they search for key evidence and piece together information to uncover the truth of who killed Kiesha. The case quickly unfolds into a complex investigation which demands relentless focus and all of the team’s expertise. Kiesha’s aunt Rachel and her best friend Bob share memories of her vibrant personality, the struggles she faced, and the heartbreak of losing her. With intimate access to the detectives and Kiesha’s loved ones, this episode reveals the personal impact of her murder and the dedicated work involved in seeking justice.

programme.title: Blade Runner
programme.desc: The 2007 final cut of Ridley Scott's sci-fi classic. Los Angeles, 2019. Mankind has succeeded in creating replicants - near-perfect humanoids superior in intelligence even to humans - but as a result of a mutiny on a human colony in outer space, it is now illegal for unlicensed replicants to be on Earth. The punishment, if they are caught, is death. Four replicants have escaped and fled back to Earth, and android hunter or 'blade runner' Deckard is charged with identifying and 'retiring' them...

programme.desc: A team of detectives arrive in the market town of Elgin tasked with investigating the brutal murder of a 32-year-old mother of two. On 16 November 2023, Lucretia ‘Kiesha’ Donaghy’s body is discovered in her home after worried friends are unable to reach her. She has been victim of a frenzied attack. We follow the detectives' every move as they search for key evidence and piece together information to uncover the truth of who killed Kiesha. The case quickly unfolds into a complex investigation which demands relentless focus and all of the team’s expertise. programme.title: James Martin's Spanish Adventure
programme.desc: Well-travelled and much-loved chef James Martin gets underneath the skin of Spain - a country he hardly knows but is excited to explore - as he discovers the history and culture of the country's diverse regions through food. It's a road trip like no other that stops at 20 destinations and travels anti-clockwise from San Sebastian to Girona through ever-changing landscapes to seek out key ingredients and sample the fine dining offerings, rustic eateries, and traditional recipes that make Spain one of the most exciting countries in the world for gastronomy. While on his journey, James will be setting up his mobile kitchen against backdrops of stunning scenery and also taking up residency in a gorgeous mountaintop villa as his Spanish 'home from home' kitchen to cook 80 mouth-watering recipes.

programme.title: Unwind with ITV
programme.desc: Your daily escape designed to calm the mind and encourage relaxation and reflection. [S]

programme.title: Ainsley's Fantastic Flavours
programme.desc: North American: Ainsley dives into the tastes and flavours of North America as Ruby Bhogal learns the secrets to the best fried chicken and Sheree Murphy makes a chicken pot pie. [SL,S] S2 Ep2

programme.title: James Martin's French Adventure
programme.desc: James's journey takes him to Pegasus Bridge - famous for the D-Day landings - which he drives across in his beloved 2CV. Normandy is peppered with orchards and dairy farms, famed as cider and calvados country, and is also home to rich and world-famous butter - James sets up his mobile kitchen in one of the many apple orchards in the area, where he prepares a dish of artichokes with hollandaise. James also meets Laurent, who gave up working in a factory to make butter the way his mum taught him, and visits the Le Pave d'Auge restaurant in one of the most beautiful towns in France, where he meets a chef who likes to cook with as much butter as he does and is served a dish of sweetbreads and salsify. James then uses calvados in a pork dish with wet walnuts - All of this inspires two indulgent dishes back home, pain au chocolat using lots of that lovely butter, and black pudding with scallops.

programme.title: Thunderball
programme.desc: The fourth entry in the James Bond film series. Led by one-eyed evil mastermind Emilio Largo, the terrorist group SPECTRE hijacks two warheads from a NATO plane and threatens widespread nuclear destruction to extort 100 million pounds. James Bond is sent to recover the warheads from the heart of Largo's lair in the Bahamas - while facing underwater attacks from sharks and men alike, he must also convince the enchanting Domino, who serves as Largo's mistress, to become a key ally in his mission.

programme.title: ITV News
programme.desc: National and international news with reports and analysis from ITV's Correspondents in the UK and around the world. [S]

programme.title: Love Your Weekend with Alan Titchmarsh
programme.desc: Alan is back and is joined on the farm this time by star of Gavin and Stacey Joanna Page, sports presenter and host of The High Performance Podcast Jake Humphrey dropping by, and India Hicks on the sofa to discuss the fascinating life of her mother Lady Pamela - there is also farmer Tom Davis, who brings along a pair of piglets to hog the limelight, and drinks expert Andy Clarke sharing his favourite tipples inspired by the movies in the Best of British feature to send off the show in style.

programme.title: Prue Leith's Cotswold Kitchen
programme.desc: Prue has invited Ellie Simmonds back for a second visit to her kitchen after the two got on so well the first time - this occasion sees Paralympic gold medallist Ellie bake a coffee and walnut cake which the two enjoy with a cup of tea and a good catch-up. While Prue's food hero is a tea producer from the Vale of Glamorgan who makes loose leave tea and Kombucha tea, she has a versatile dish on the menu - a baked feta, roasted tomatoes and garlic dish which can be used as a starter with bread dipped into it. Prue then adds spinach and cooked pasta, gives it a good mix and serves it as a main course as John heads off to see Hamish Mackie, a local bronze sculptor and good friend who lets John have a go at creating an ornamental elephant. programme.desc: James's journey takes him to Pegasus Bridge - famous for the D-Day landings - which he drives across in his beloved 2CV. programme.title: Prue Leith's Cotswold Kitchen
programme.desc: Prue has invited Ellie Simmonds back for a second visit to her kitchen after the two got on so well the first time - this occasion sees Paralympic gold medallist Ellie bake a coffee and walnut cake which the two enjoy with a cup of tea and a good catch-up. While Prue's food hero is a tea producer from the Vale of Glamorgan who makes loose leave tea and Kombucha tea, she has a versatile dish on the menu - a baked feta, roasted tomatoes and garlic dish which can be used as a starter with bread dipped into it. Prue then adds spinach and cooked pasta, gives it a good mix and serves it as a main course as John heads off to see Hamish Mackie, a local bronze sculptor and good friend who lets John have a go at creating an ornamental elephant. Prue is pleased with herself when a hack for picking up egg yolks goes very well - she's joined in the kitchen by John for chicken ramen and spicy edamame as the two take a trip down memory lane to a holiday in Japan when they tried many types of ramen.

programme.title: James Martin's Spanish Adventure
programme.desc: Well-travelled and much-loved chef James Martin gets underneath the skin of Spain - a country he hardly knows but is excited to explore - as he discovers the history and culture of the country's diverse regions through food. It's a road trip like no other that stops at 20 destinations and travels anti-clockwise from San Sebastian to Girona through ever-changing landscapes to seek out key ingredients and sample the fine dining offerings, rustic eateries, and traditional recipes that make Spain one of the most exciting countries in the world for gastronomy. While on his journey, James will be setting up his mobile kitchen against backdrops of stunning scenery and also taking up residency in a gorgeous mountaintop villa as his Spanish 'home from home' kitchen to cook 80 mouth-watering recipes.

programme.title: James Martin's French Adventure
programme.desc: James's journey takes him to Pegasus Bridge - famous for the D-Day landings - which he drives across in his beloved 2CV. Normandy is peppered with orchards and dairy farms, famed as cider and calvados country, and is also home to rich and world-famous butter - James sets up his mobile kitchen in one of the many apple orchards in the area, where he prepares a dish of artichokes with hollandaise. James also meets Laurent, who gave up working in a factory to make butter the way his mum taught him, and visits the Le Pave d'Auge restaurant in one of the most beautiful towns in France, where he meets a chef who likes to cook with as much butter as he does and is served a dish of sweetbreads and salsify. James then uses calvados in a pork dish with wet walnuts - All of this inspires two indulgent dishes back home, pain au chocolat using lots of that lovely butter, and black pudding with scallops.

programme.title: Thunderball

programme.title: Love Your Weekend with Alan Titchmarsh
programme.desc: Alan is back and is joined on the farm this time by star of Gavin and Stacey Joanna Page, sports presenter and host of The High Performance Podcast Jake Humphrey dropping by, and India Hicks on the sofa to discuss the fascinating life of her mother Lady Pamela - there is also farmer Tom Davis, who brings along a pair of piglets to hog the limelight, and drinks expert Andy Clarke sharing his favourite tipples inspired by the movies in the Best of British feature to send off the show in style.

programme.title: Prue Leith's Cotswold Kitchen
programme.desc: Prue has invited Ellie Simmonds back for a second visit to her kitchen after the two got on so well the first time - this occasion sees Paralympic gold medallist Ellie bake a coffee and walnut cake which the two enjoy with a cup of tea and a good catch-up. While Prue's food hero is a tea producer from the Vale of Glamorgan who makes loose leave tea and Kombucha tea, she has a versatile dish on the menu - a baked feta, roasted tomatoes and garlic dish which can be used as a starter with bread dipped into it. Prue then adds spinach and cooked pasta, gives it a good mix and serves it as a main course as John heads off to see Hamish Mackie, a local bronze sculptor and good friend who lets John have a go at creating an ornamental elephant. Prue is pleased with herself when a hack for picking up egg yolks goes very well - she's joined in the kitchen by John for chicken ramen and spicy edamame as the two take a trip down memory lane to a holiday in Japan when they tried many types of ramen.

programme.title: Prue Leith's Cotswold Kitchen
programme.desc: Prue has invited Ellie Simmonds back for a second visit to her kitchen after the two got on so well the first time - this occasion sees Paralympic gold medallist Ellie bake a coffee and walnut cake which the two enjoy with a cup of tea and a good catch-up. While Prue's food hero is a tea producer from the Vale of Glamorgan who makes loose leave tea and Kombucha tea, she has a versatile dish on the menu - a baked feta, roasted tomatoes and garlic dish which can be used as a starter with bread dipped into it. Prue then adds spinach and cooked pasta, gives it a good mix and serves it as a main course as John heads off to see Hamish Mackie, a local bronze sculptor and good friend who lets John have a go at creating an ornamental elephant. Prue is pleased with herself when a hack for picking up egg yolks goes very well - she's joined in the kitchen by John for chicken ramen and spicy edamame as the two take a trip down memory lane to a holiday in Japan when they tried many types of ramen.

programme.title: Love Your Garden
programme.desc: Alan Titchmarsh, landscape artist David Domoney, and horticulturalists Katie Rushworth and Frances Tophill travel the country to come to the rescue of people who need their help in making the most of their outdoor spaces. Alan and the team transform barren plots and small neglected pieces of ground into stunning gardens and outdoor areas for relaxation while informing and inspiring viewers on how to recreate the looks themselves. Each episode sees Alan surprise garden owners who have an inspiring story to tell and whose outdoor space is in desperate need of a transformation - while the owner is whisked away out of sight, Alan designs the new-look garden by taking inspiration from the best gardens in the area and asking for help from local people and the owner's friends in completing the project.

programme.title: James Martin's Spanish Adventure
programme.desc: Well-travelled and much-loved chef James Martin gets underneath the skin of Spain - a country he hardly knows but is excited to explore - as he discovers the history and culture of the country's diverse regions through food. It's a road trip like no other that stops at 20 destinations and travels anti-clockwise from San Sebastian to Girona through ever-changing landscapes to seek out key ingredients and sample the fine dining offerings, rustic eateries, and traditional recipes that make Spain one of the most exciting countries in the world for gastronomy. While on his journey, James will be setting up his mobile kitchen against backdrops of stunning scenery and also taking up residency in a gorgeous mountaintop villa as his Spanish 'home from home' kitchen to cook 80 mouth-watering recipes.

programme.title: James Martin's French Adventure
programme.desc: James's journey takes him to Pegasus Bridge - famous for the D-Day landings - which he drives across in his beloved 2CV. Normandy is peppered with orchards and dairy farms, famed as cider and calvados country, and is also home to rich and world-famous butter - James sets up his mobile kitchen in one of the many apple orchards in the area, where he prepares a dish of artichokes with hollandaise. James also meets Laurent, who gave up working in a factory to make butter the way his mum taught him, and visits the Le Pave d'Auge restaurant in one of the most beautiful towns in France, where he meets a chef who likes to cook with as much butter as he does and is served a dish of sweetbreads and salsify. James then uses calvados in a pork dish with wet walnuts - All of this inspires two indulgent dishes back home, pain au chocolat using lots of that lovely butter, and black pudding with scallops.

programme.title: Thunderball
programme.desc: The fourth entry in the James Bond film series. Led by one-eyed evil mastermind Emilio Largo, the terrorist group SPECTRE hijacks two warheads from a NATO plane and threatens widespread nuclear destruction to extort 100 million pounds. James Bond is sent to recover the warheads from the heart of Largo's lair in the Bahamas - while facing underwater attacks from sharks and men alike, he must also convince the enchanting Domino, who serves as Largo's mistress, to become a key ally in his mission.

Alan and the team transform barren plots and small neglected pieces of ground into stunning gardens and outdoor areas for relaxation while informing and inspiring viewers on how to recreate the looks themselves. Each episode sees Alan surprise garden owners who have an inspiring story to tell and whose outdoor space is in desperate need of a transformation - while the owner is whisked away out of sight, Alan designs the new-look garden by taking inspiration from the best gardens in the area and asking for help from local people and the owner's friends in completing the project.

programme.title: James Martin's Spanish Adventure
programme.desc: Well-travelled and much-loved chef James Martin gets underneath the skin of Spain - a country he hardly knows but is excited to explore - as he discovers the history and culture of the country's diverse regions through food. It's a road trip like no other that stops at 20 destinations and travels anti-clockwise from San Sebastian to Girona through ever-changing landscapes to seek out key ingredients and sample the fine dining offerings, rustic eateries, and traditional recipes that make Spain one of the most exciting countries in the world for gastronomy. While on his journey, James will be setting up his mobile kitchen against backdrops of stunning scenery and also taking up residency in a gorgeous mountaintop villa as his Spanish 'home from home' kitchen to cook 80 mouth-watering recipes.

programme.title: James Martin's French Adventure
programme.desc: James's journey takes him to Pegasus Bridge - famous for the D-Day landings - which he drives across in his beloved 2CV. Normandy is peppered with orchards and dairy farms, famed as cider and calvados country, and is also home to rich and world-famous butter - James sets up his mobile kitchen in one of the many apple orchards in the area, where he prepares a dish of artichokes with hollandaise. James also meets Laurent, who gave up working in a factory to make butter the way his mum taught him, and visits the Le Pave d'Auge restaurant in one of the most beautiful towns in France, where he meets a chef who likes to cook with as much butter as he does and is served a dish of sweetbreads and salsify. James then uses calvados in a pork dish with wet walnuts - All of this inspires two indulgent dishes back home, pain au chocolat using lots of that lovely butter, and black pudding with scallops.

programme.title: Thunderball
programme.desc: The fourth entry in the James Bond film series. Led by one-eyed evil mastermind Emilio Largo, the terrorist group SPECTRE hijacks two warheads from a NATO plane and threatens widespread nuclear destruction to extort 100 million pounds. James Bond is sent to recover the warheads from the heart of Largo's lair in the Bahamas - while facing underwater attacks from sharks and men alike, he must also convince the enchanting Domino, who serves as Largo's mistress, to become a key ally in his mission.

programme.title: ITV News
programme.desc: National and international news with reports and analysis from ITV's Correspondents in the UK and around the world. [S,HD]

programme.title: Love Your Weekend with Alan Titchmarsh
programme.desc: Alan is back and is joined on the farm this time by star of Gavin and Stacey Joanna Page, sports presenter and host of The High Performance Podcast Jake Humphrey dropping by, and India Hicks on the sofa to discuss the fascinating life of her mother Lady Pamela - there is also farmer Tom Davis, who brings along a pair of piglets to hog the limelight, and drinks expert Andy Clarke sharing his favourite tipples inspired by the movies in the Best of British feature to send off the show in style.

programme.title: Prue Leith's Cotswold Kitchen
programme.desc: Prue has invited Ellie Simmonds back for a second visit to her kitchen after the two got on so well the first time - this occasion sees Paralympic gold medallist Ellie bake a coffee and walnut cake which the two enjoy with a cup of tea and a good catch-up. While Prue's food hero is a tea producer from the Vale of Glamorgan who makes loose leave tea and Kombucha tea, she has a versatile dish on the menu - a baked feta, roasted tomatoes and garlic dish which can be used as a starter with bread dipped into it. Prue then adds spinach and cooked pasta, gives it a good mix and serves it as a main course as John heads off to see Hamish Mackie, a local bronze sculptor and good friend who lets John have a go at creating an ornamental elephant. Prue is pleased with herself when a hack for picking up egg yolks goes very well - she's joined in the kitchen by John for chicken ramen and spicy edamame as the two take a trip down memory lane to a holiday in Japan when they tried many types of ramen.

programme.title: James Martin's French Adventure
programme.desc: James's journey takes him to Pegasus Bridge - famous for the D-Day landings - which he drives across in his beloved 2CV. Normandy is peppered with orchards and dairy farms, famed as cider and calvados country, and is also home to rich and world-famous butter - James sets up his mobile kitchen in one of the many apple orchards in the area, where he prepares a dish of artichokes with hollandaise. James also meets Laurent, who gave up working in a factory to make butter the way his mum taught him, and visits the Le Pave d'Auge restaurant in one of the most beautiful towns in France, where he meets a chef who likes to cook with as much butter as he does and is served a dish of sweetbreads and salsify. James then uses calvados in a pork dish with wet walnuts - All of this inspires two indulgent dishes back home, pain au chocolat using lots of that lovely butter, and black pudding with scallops.

programme.title: Thunderball
programme.desc: The fourth entry in the James Bond film series. Led by one-eyed evil mastermind Emilio Largo, the terrorist group SPECTRE hijacks two warheads from a NATO plane and threatens widespread nuclear destruction to extort 100 million pounds. James Bond is sent to recover the warheads from the heart of Largo's lair in the Bahamas - while facing underwater attacks from sharks and men alike, he must also convince the enchanting Domino, who serves as Largo's mistress, to become a key ally in his mission.

programme.title: Love Your Weekend with Alan Titchmarsh
programme.desc: Alan is back and is joined on the farm this time by star of Gavin and Stacey Joanna Page, sports presenter and host of The High Performance Podcast Jake Humphrey dropping by, and India Hicks on the sofa to discuss the fascinating life of her mother Lady Pamela - there is also farmer Tom Davis, who brings along a pair of piglets to hog the limelight, and drinks expert Andy Clarke sharing his favourite tipples inspired by the movies in the Best of British feature to send off the show in style.

programme.title: Prue Leith's Cotswold Kitchen
programme.desc: Prue has invited Ellie Simmonds back for a second visit to her kitchen after the two got on so well the first time - this occasion sees Paralympic gold medallist Ellie bake a coffee and walnut cake which the two enjoy with a cup of tea and a good catch-up. While Prue's food hero is a tea producer from the Vale of Glamorgan who makes loose leave tea and Kombucha tea, she has a versatile dish on the menu - a baked feta, roasted tomatoes and garlic dish which can be used as a starter with bread dipped into it. Prue then adds spinach and cooked pasta, gives it a good mix and serves it as a main course as John heads off to see Hamish Mackie, a local bronze sculptor and good friend who lets John have a go at creating an ornamental elephant. Prue is pleased with herself when a hack for picking up egg yolks goes very well - she's joined in the kitchen by John for chicken ramen and spicy edamame as the two take a trip down memory lane to a holiday in Japan when they tried many types of ramen.

programme.title: Love Your Garden
programme.desc: Alan Titchmarsh, landscape artist David Domoney, and horticulturalists Katie Rushworth and Frances Tophill travel the country to come to the rescue of people who need their help in making the most of their outdoor spaces. Alan and the team transform barren plots and small neglected pieces of ground into stunning gardens and outdoor areas for relaxation while informing and inspiring viewers on how to recreate the looks themselves. Each episode sees Alan surprise garden owners who have an inspiring story to tell and whose outdoor space is in desperate need of a transformation - while the owner is whisked away out of sight, Alan designs the new-look garden by taking inspiration from the best gardens in the area and asking for help from local people and the owner's friends in completing the project.

programme.title: James Martin's Spanish Adventure
programme.desc: Well-travelled and much-loved chef James Martin gets underneath the skin of Spain - a country he hardly knows but is excited to explore - as he discovers the history and culture of the country's diverse regions through food. It's a road trip like no other that stops at 20 destinations and travels anti-clockwise from San Sebastian to Girona through ever-changing landscapes to seek out key ingredients and sample the fine dining offerings, rustic eateries, and traditional recipes that make Spain one of the most exciting countries in the world for gastronomy. While on his journey, James will be setting up his mobile kitchen against backdrops of stunning scenery and also taking up residency in a gorgeous mountaintop villa as his Spanish 'home from home' kitchen to cook 80 mouth-watering recipes.

programme.title: G'wed
programme.desc: When Christopher's posh old schoolmates arrive for the National Debating Championships final, the Scouse lads fear losing him to his old world. Instead, the groups begin to bond until a drunken factory break-in, crashed forklift and night in the cells forces Christopher to confront where he belongs. In the debate final, Christopher delivers a personal argument about why people divide themselves and how belonging to two worlds can be a strength. Meanwhile, Anna's return fractures Aimee and Wayne's alliance when she offers a different version of the past, leaving Aimee torn between loyalty to her dad and the mum she never stopped missing. Lewis's redemption arc implodes when his public apology tour exposes more chaos than growth, forcing Kieron to stage an intervention.

programme.title: Piglets
programme.desc: Sitcom set in a charmingly dysfunctional police training college. B Group learn how to deal with missing persons and discover the crucial importance of the golden hour - meanwhile, two new recruits join the class in the form of the irrepressible Danni, who is soon to be married and will not let anyone forget it, and Connor, an enigmatic teller of very tall tales. Still struggling to knock the trainees into shape, Superintendents Bob Weekes and Julie Spry find themselves competing to accompany Chief Superintendent Cunningham to a conference in the Bahamas - elsewhere, Sergeant Daz Black is on a final warning about his violent conduct and must undergo anger management sessions as Julie assigns him to a course of therapy from the slightly under-qualified Melanie that makes him even angrier, and Student Officer Paul Huggins has been exposed as a mole (or 'prune in the nest') placed in the college by his criminal family and is now forced to work for the police as a 'double prune'.

programme.title: James Martin's Spanish Adventure
programme.desc: Well-travelled and much-loved chef James Martin gets underneath the skin of Spain - a country he hardly knows but is excited to explore - as he discovers the history and culture of the country's diverse regions through food. It's a road trip like no other that stops at 20 destinations and travels anti-clockwise from San Sebastian to Girona through ever-changing landscapes to seek out key ingredients and sample the fine dining offerings, rustic eateries, and traditional recipes that make Spain one of the most exciting countries in the world for gastronomy. While on his journey, James will be setting up his mobile kitchen against backdrops of stunning scenery and also taking up residency in a gorgeous mountaintop villa as his Spanish 'home from home' kitchen to cook 80 mouth-watering recipes.

programme.title: James Martin's French Adventure
programme.desc: James's journey takes him to Pegasus Bridge - famous for the D-Day landings - which he drives across in his beloved 2CV. Normandy is peppered with orchards and dairy farms, famed as cider and calvados country, and is also home to rich and world-famous butter - James sets up his mobile kitchen in one of the many apple orchards in the area, where he prepares a dish of artichokes with hollandaise. James also meets Laurent, who gave up working in a factory to make butter the way his mum taught him, and visits the Le Pave d'Auge restaurant in one of the most beautiful towns in France, where he meets a chef who likes to cook with as much butter as he does and is served a dish of sweetbreads and salsify. James then uses calvados in a pork dish with wet walnuts - All of this inspires two indulgent dishes back home, pain au chocolat using lots of that lovely butter, and black pudding with scallops.

Led by one-eyed evil mastermind Emilio Largo, the terrorist group SPECTRE hijacks two warheads from a NATO plane and threatens widespread nuclear destruction to extort 100 million pounds. James Bond is sent to recover the warheads from the heart of Largo's lair in the Bahamas - while facing underwater attacks from sharks and men alike, he must also convince the enchanting Domino, who serves as Largo's mistress, to become a key ally in his mission.

programme.title: Prue Leith's Cotswold Kitchen
programme.desc: Prue has invited Ellie Simmonds back for a second visit to her kitchen after the two got on so well the first time - this occasion sees Paralympic gold medallist Ellie bake a coffee and walnut cake which the two enjoy with a cup of tea and a good catch-up. While Prue's food hero is a tea producer from the Vale of Glamorgan who makes loose leave tea and Kombucha tea, she has a versatile dish on the menu - a baked feta, roasted tomatoes and garlic dish which can be used as a starter with bread dipped into it. Prue then adds spinach and cooked pasta, gives it a good mix and serves it as a main course as John heads off to see Hamish Mackie, a local bronze sculptor and good friend who lets John have a go at creating an ornamental elephant. Prue is pleased with herself when a hack for picking up egg yolks goes very well - she's joined in the kitchen by John for chicken ramen and spicy edamame as the two take a trip down memory lane to a holiday in Japan when they tried many types of ramen.

programme.title: Love Your Garden
programme.desc: Alan Titchmarsh, landscape artist David Domoney, and horticulturalists Katie Rushworth and Frances Tophill travel the country to come to the rescue of people who need their help in making the most of their outdoor spaces. Alan and the team transform barren plots and small neglected pieces of ground into stunning gardens and outdoor areas for relaxation while informing and inspiring viewers on how to recreate the looks themselves. Each episode sees Alan surprise garden owners who have an inspiring story to tell and whose outdoor space is in desperate need of a transformation - while the owner is whisked away out of sight, Alan designs the new-look garden by taking inspiration from the best gardens in the area and asking for help from local people and the owner's friends in completing the project.
